newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian police free opposition chiefs.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian police free opposition chiefs.

text.p: Nigerian police have freed three opposition leaders detained since June in an investigation into the murder of the wife of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola, an opposition spokesman said on Tuesday.

Abraham Adesanya, 74, Ayo Adebanjo, 68 and Ganiyu Dawodu, 63, all prominent members of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) group, were detained to help police inquiry into the murder of Kudirat Abiola, who was shot in the head while driving along a Lagos street in June.
"They were freed last night by the police after the order of the Lagos high court," NADECO's Joe Aladeshoun told Reuters.
Last Friday Judge Abdul Kafarati of Lagos high court ruled that the arrest and detention of the three was unlawful inspite of a police appeal that they should still be held.
The court initially ruled the detention of the three men unlawful but the police appealed against the court ruling.
"They have not been charged since they were arrested and we are naturally happy that they have regained their freedom," Aladeshoun said.
Abiola's vocal wife had led the campaign to free him and install him as president in line with the results of a 1993 election, annulled by a former military government.
NADECO has also been campaigning for the military rulers to release Abiola, detained since 1994 when he declared himself president in defiance of the military rulers.
